title: Center of a Star
statement:
A **star** network has one **center** node connected to every other node, and no other connections. There are `n` nodes labelled `1` to `n`, and `edges` lists the `n - 1` connections, each as `[a, b]` meaning nodes `a` and `b` are directly connected.

Return the **label of the center node**.
constraints: len(edges) = n - 1, and the edges form a star

examples.explanation: Node 2 is connected to all the others.

hints.nudge: The center is in every edge. Two different edges share exactly one node. Which one?
hints.pattern: You only need the first two edges.
hints.pseudocode:
[a, b] = edges[0]; [c, d] = edges[1]
return a if a is c or d else b
hints.walkthrough: Counting how many edges each node appears in works in O(n) (the center appears n - 1 times). But the center belongs to every edge, so it must be the node shared by any two edges. Look only at the first two edges: whichever node of the first edge also occurs in the second edge is the center. That is O(1).
